subtopics.title: Two Kinds of Change — the Deciding Question

questions.question: The single question that classifies any change is:
In a physical change, the particles of the substance:
options: Remain unchanged — only their arrangement, spacing or energy changes

questions.question: In a chemical change:
options: Bonds are broken and new bonds form — atoms regroup into new substances with different properties
The substance can always be recovered by cooling

questions.question: Chemical changes are usually hard to reverse because:
options: They happen too fast to catch
They only occur at high temperature
Reversal is illegal in a closed container
The original substance no longer exists — it has been rebuilt into new substances

subtopics.title: Physical Change Up Close — Same Particles, New Arrangement

questions.question: Boiling water is a physical change because:
options: The intact water molecules merely gain enough energy to escape as steam — no new substance forms
Water splits into hydrogen and oxygen

questions.question: Dissolving salt in water is physical because:
options: The ions and water molecules all survive unchanged — evaporation returns identical salt
The salt reacts with the water
Salt water is a new substance
The salt is destroyed and remade

questions.question: Iron filings mixed with sulfur powder, unheated, form a:
options: Mixture — a physical combination; a magnet still pulls the iron straight out

questions.question: An energy change during a change of state proves:
options: Nothing about classification on its own — physical changes also absorb or release energy; only a new substance proves chemistry

subtopics.title: Chemical Change Up Close — New Substances, and the Evidence

questions.question: The five signs of chemical change are:
options: Gas produced, precipitate formed, permanent colour change, self-caused temperature change, light or sound emitted

questions.question: A precipitate is:
options: A gas released from a liquid
An insoluble solid that appears when two clear solutions react

questions.question: A reaction that releases heat, and one that absorbs heat, are called respectively:
Bubbles alone do not prove a chemical change because:
options: Boiling also makes bubbles, and boiling is physical — the verdict still needs a new substance

subtopics.title: Mass, Energy and the Tricky Cases

questions.question: Burning wood seems to lose mass, but the law of conservation of mass holds because:
options: The escaping smoke and gases carry the missing mass — trapped and weighed, the books balance
Ash weighs the same as wood
The law only applies to physical changes

questions.question: Boiling water versus passing an electric current through water:
options: Boiling is physical — steam is still water; electrolysis is chemical — hydrogen and oxygen are new substances
Boiling is chemical; electrolysis is physical

questions.question: A fizzing headache tablet in water is a chemical change because:
options: The fizz is new carbon dioxide gas that did not exist in the tablet before

questions.question: The direction of energy flow — released or absorbed — tells you:
options: Nothing about the classification — only the new-substance question decides

subtopics.title: The Ice Tray and the Braai Fire

questions.question: The ice tray scene shows physical change because the water:
options: Can be frozen and melted over and over, staying water at every stage
Becomes a new substance when frozen

questions.question: The braai fire scene shows chemical change because the wood:
options: No longer exists — it has become ash, smoke and gases, and no simple process brings it back

questions.question: The take-home test from the two scenes is:
options: If the change was hot, it was chemical
If the change was fast, it was chemical
If the change happened outdoors, it was physical
If the original can be recovered by simple means — cooling, evaporating, sieving — the change was physical

questions.question: Rust on a garden gate is a chemical clue because the colour change:
options: Is only on the surface paint
Goes deep and cannot be undone — the iron has become a different substance
Matches the colour of the soil

questions.question: Fresh cement warming itself for hours is evidence of:
options: A reaction releasing energy as new bonds form — heat nobody added

questions.question: A fried egg is a chemical change because the white:
options: Turns solid and stays solid forever — a new substance with new properties

subtopics.title: The Candle Doing Both at Once

questions.question: The wax melting at the top of a burning candle is:
options: Physical — the cooled wax hardens back into wax, unchanged

questions.question: The wax burning at the wick is chemical because it:
options: Becomes carbon dioxide and water vapour — new substances that never return to wax

questions.question: Even in the burning, weighing the candle and all captured gases shows:
options: Mass is destroyed by the flame
Mass increases as light is absorbed
The total mass balances exactly — atoms regroup but never vanish: conservation of mass
